orientation: Scan is 792x1224 pt portrait with the landscape sheet rotated: the title block is along the bottom edge and text runs bottom-to-top. Rotate the scan 90 degrees COUNTER-CLOCKWISE to read upright (title block then sits on the right, as drawn). All coordinates in this file are UNROTATED scan page points (MuPDF page space, origin top-left, y down), so they can be used directly with page.get_pixmap(clip=...). Page /Rotate is 0; the rotation is baked into the raster.
feature: Bill's marks: every printed opening tag he highlighted (window-type hexagons, door-number circles), plus his pen notes and the hand tally by the title block
source: human-confirmed by eye: every mark rendered at 4.5x (324 dpi, 20-pt grid tiles p0_tile_r*c*.png) and ambiguous ones at 6x-12x (p0_*_zoom/sat.png) in out/verify/2026-08-22/bill-truth/work/; transcribed 2026-08-22. Positions +/-5 pt. Independently re-checked against Bill's own handwritten tally on the same sheet (bill_tally below) and against his three supplier takeoffs (see TRUTH.md).
convention: From this sheet set's own FLOOR SYMBOLS legend (A-2.10): a CIRCLE with a 3-digit number is a (N) DOOR SYMBOL = door number from the door schedule; a HEXAGON with a letter is a (N) WINDOW SYMBOL = window/storefront type from the window schedule. Bill highlights the printed tag of every opening in his trade (windows, balcony doors, interior storefront doors 100-107, exterior storefront N-Z with doors 004/005). He does NOT number openings himself: the numbers on the sheets are the architect's door numbers. On the residential floors he then writes one count per type beside the title block; on A-2.00/A-2.10 he lists the interior-storefront door numbers instead. Highlighter colour is his per-type key and is not consistent across sheets (D is pink on A-2.20, H is green on A-2.30 and yellow on A-2.40), so read the printed code, not the colour.
coordinate_note: x,y = centre of the printed tag in unrotated scan points, +/-5 pt. kind: window-tag = printed hexagon, door-tag = printed circle, hand = Bill's pen. attached_to: room/wall read from the nearest printed labels; for A-2.20/A-2.30 the UNIT numbers are inferred from the identical layout on A-2.40/A-2.50 where the labels were read in the same tiles, and should be treated as approximate.
